UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                      FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission          )
Complainant                                     )                    Docket No. EL26-98-000
                                                )
v.                                              )
                                                )
PJM Interconnection, LLC.,                      )
Respondent                                      )

                   UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME OF
                    PENNSYLVANIA PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION

        Pursuant to Rules 212, 213, and 2008 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission,1 the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission (PA

PUC) respectfully requests a 29-day extension of time to November 12, 2026 to answer the

September 29, 2026 Motion to Dismiss of PJM Interconnection, LLC (PJM). Commission Rule

2008 authorizes extensions of time for “good cause” shown, which exists here.2 PJM has

authorized PA PUC to represent that PJM is unopposed to PA PUC’s requested extension.

        Commission Rule 213 provides that an answer to a motion must be made within 15 days

after the motion is filed.3 As PJM filed its Motion to Dismiss on September 29, 2026, PA PUC’s

answer thereto is presently due on October 14, 2026. Consistent with Commission Rule 213, PA

PUC requests a modest 29-day extension of time, until November 12, 2026, to prepare a

thorough response to PJM’s Motion to Dismiss.4



1
  18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212, .213, & .2008 (2026).
2
  18 C.F.R. § 385.2008.
3
  18 C.F.R. § 385.213(d)(1).
4
  18 C.F.R. § 385.213(d)(1)(i).

                                                1
        The Commission should grant PA PUC’s requested 29-day extension because it is an

insufficient timeframe for PA PUC to fully respond to PJM’s claims of alleged deficiencies in PA

PUC’s Section 206 Complaint, while accommodating PA PUC’s handling of pressing regulatory

matters. The PA PUC, as a state regulatory agency, and its counsel are currently engaged in handling

other pressing business. Further, the Commission’s normal 15-day response period is interrupted by a

Federal holiday which precedes the current October 14, 2026 answer date. As such, in this

circumstance, the normal 15-day timeframe detrimentally impacts the PA PUC’s ability to

thoroughly respond to PJM’s Motion to Dismiss. The requested extension will allow PA PUC to

thoroughly respond to the factual and legal claims set forth in PJM’s Motion to Dismiss.

       Additionally, a 29-day extension of time will not affect PJM’s market efficiency planning

cycle or otherwise delay any imminent action. In its own Unopposed Motion for Extension of Time,

wherein it sought an additional 21 days to respond to PA PUC’s Section 206 complaint, PJM asserted

that “the requested extension will not affect PJM’s administration of the next market efficiency

planning cycle. The proposal window for the 2026/2027 market efficiency cycle is not currently

expected to open until the first Quarter of 2027 and is expected to remain open through the second

Quarter of 2027. PJM currently expects to complete its analysis of the proposed solutions in

November 2027, followed by a first read to stakeholders in December 2027, a second read in January

2028, and consideration by the PJM Board of Managers in February 2028.” Likewise, extending PA

PUC’s answer deadline by 29 days will not affect any proposal, evaluation, stakeholder review, or

project selection deadline in PJM’s forthcoming market efficiency planning cycle. If the requested is

granted, PA PUC’s answer will be filed months before PJM’s next proposal window opens and more

than a year before PJM is expected to complete its analysis that is the subject of the PA PUC’s

Section 206 complaint.

       In conclusion, the default fifteen-day answer period is insufficient for PA PUC to fully

respond to PJM’s claims of alleged deficiencies PA PUC’s Section 206 Complaint. The requested

                                                  2
 extension to September 29, 2026, will allow PA PUC to develop a meaningful answer that fully

responds to statements made in PJM’s Motion to Dismiss, while managing its other pressing

obligations. Additionally, an extension of time will not affect PJM’s market efficiency planning

cycle or otherwise delay any imminent action. Moreover, as PJM noted, the Commission has granted

motions to extend response deadlines in similar circumstances.5 Further, as previously noted, the

Commission granted PJM itself a 21-day extension to respond to the PA PUC’s Section 206

Complaint in the instant proceeding for similar reasons.6

        Accordingly, the PA PUC requests that the Commission grant this motion for extension of

time on or before October 9, 2026, which will allow PA PUC to properly plan to file an answer by

the original date of October 14, 2026, if so required.



                                                    Respectfully submitted,

                                                    /s/ Kriss E. Brown
                                                    Kriss E. Brown
                                                    Executive Deputy Chief Counsel
